chunks: From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible to buy green crops?' He said, 'Yes, there is no objection to it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: no objection to it / it is permissible
key_terms.ٱلْأَخْضَرِ: green (referring to crops still in the field)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy crops while they are still green in the field according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Bukayr ibn A'yan inquires of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the validity of purchasing 'green crops' (al-zar' al-akhdar), which refers to crops still standing in the field before harvest. The Imam’s affirmative response ('Yes, no harm in it') establishes the permissibility of this transaction, distinguishing it from sales involving uncertainty (gharar) by affirming that the produce is considered a tangible asset even while growing. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for agricultural trade, allowing farmers to secure liquidity before the actual harvest occurs.
